text.p: Amoco Chemical Europe Tuesday hosted commissioning ceremonies for a 200,000 metric-ton polypropylene unit, the second unit to be located in Beel, Belgium, the Amoco Corp subsidiary said in a statement released in New York.
The unit has full capabilities to produce homopolymer, random copolymer and impact copolymer utilizing Amoco's CD catalyst.
"It brings Amoco Europe's total polypropylene capacity to 410,000 metric tons, and represents another extension of the Amoco gas phase process," Amoco Chemical said.
"With only two minor modifications, we expect to be able to operate at 280,000 tons within two or three years."
On a world-wide basis, Amoco said, it is the second largest polypropylene producer. Amoco's North American-based annual polypropylene capacity stands at 815,000 metric tons.

Plans for a new North American unit are nearing completion with earliest start-up in January 1999, it said. Development of Asian capacity and numerous worldwide gas phase process licensing opportunities are also being vigorously explored.

Amoco said engineering and construction of the new unit was accomplished by Technip SA. It was completed in less than 19 months from start of engineering under the expected cost, Amoco said. Catalyst was introduced in early September, three days after mechanical completion.

After one week of operation, the unit was producing specification homopolymer at design rates. In mid-September, the unit successfully and easily transitioned to impact copolymer, the company said. This represents Amoco's first entry into European copolymer supply for the packaging, consumer and industrial segments.
